% A heading right after another heading has only the space below the
% first, as LaTeX's \@startsection adds no space above a heading while
% \if@nobreak holds: a section after a part, a subsection after a section,
% the same with a \label between them, starred headings with a \label,
% a subsubsection after a subsection, a run-in paragraph after a
% subsubsection, a section after a starred part with a \label, and a
% subsection after a section with an \index entry.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{makeidx}
\makeindex
\setcounter{secnumdepth}{4}
\begin{document}
Some text before the first part.
\part{Beginnings}
\section{After the part}
Some text in the section.
\section{A section}
\subsection{After the section}
Some text in the subsection.
\section{A labeled section}\label{labeled}
\subsection{After the label}
Some text in the subsection.
\section*{A starred section}\label{starred}
\subsection*{After the starred label}
Some text in the subsection.
\subsection{A subsection}
\subsubsection{After the subsection}
Some text in the subsubsection.
\subsubsection{A subsubsection}
\paragraph{A paragraph} Some text run into the paragraph's heading.
\part*{An unnumbered part}\label{unnumbered}
\section{After the unnumbered part}
Some text in the section.
\section{An indexed section}\index{indexed}
\subsection{After the index}
Some text in the subsection.
\end{document}
